description: Suspension of the license issuing process for the implementation of the terrestrial analog system channels
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2025-11-24 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - 24 television channels, including 5 state media channels, are operating in the country using licenses issued to 16 institutions by now to operate channels under the existing analog terrestrial television technology in Sri Lanka. At present, television channels are operating using the maximum capacity of the frequency spectrum, and the Ministry in charge of the subject of Mass Media has initiated the Digital Terrestrial Television Broadcasting Project in 2025, enabling to implement a single digital terrestrial broadcasting system with the aim of providing a high-quality digital experience to television viewers under modern technology, instead of the 46-year-old analog terrestrial television broadcasting system. An Agreement has been entered into between the Government of Sri Lanka and the Government of Japan for this purpose, and the project is scheduled to be completed in 2029. Since the old analog terrestrial television broadcasting system is scheduled to be completely shut down after 02 years from the completion of the project, it has been observed that further issuance of licenses through the same is not effective. Accordingly, the joint proposal made by the Hon. President in his capacity as the Minister of Digital Economy and the Minister of Health and Mass Media to suspend with immediate effect the process of allocating frequencies from the frequency spectrum for the terrestrial operation of television channels by the Telecommunications Regulatory Commission of Sri Lanka and the process of issuing licenses for the terrestrial operation of television channels by the Ministry of Health and Mass Media, was approved by the Cabinet.
